words.textHint: You bend your knees and push off the ground so both feet go up in the air.
Moving your legs as fast as you can, much faster than walking.
Moving on your hands and knees like a baby does.
Walking very quietly on just the front part of your feet.
Reaching your arms way up high to make your body long, like when you wake up.
Turning around and around in circles until you get dizzy.
Hitting your two hands together to make noise when you like a show.
Moving your hand back and forth in the air to say hello or goodbye.
Moving your body to the beat when music is playing.
Hitting a ball with your foot, like in soccer.
Using your arm to make a ball fly through the air to someone else.
Grabbing a ball with your hands when someone tosses it to you.
Using your hands and feet to go up a tree or a ladder.
Moving your arms and legs to travel through the water in a pool.
Bouncing up and down on one foot, or how a bunny moves.
A happy bouncy way of moving where you step and hop, step and hop.
What you do on a chair when your legs are tired.
Closing your eyes in bed at night and dreaming until morning.
Putting food in your mouth, chewing it, and swallowing it.
Swallowing water or juice from a cup when you are thirsty.
What you do to your teeth every morning and night with a little tool and paste.
Cleaning your hands with soap and water before dinner.
Tipping a pitcher so juice or milk goes into a cup.
Bending clean laundry or paper neatly in half again and again.
Using scissors to make paper into two pieces.
Making a picture on paper with crayons or a pencil.
Making a colorful picture using a brush dipped in wet colors.
Looking at the words in a book to find out what the story says.
Making letters and words on paper with a pencil.
What you do with your voice to make the words of a song sound like music.
Talking in a very very quiet voice so only one person can hear you.
Using your loudest voice so people far away can hear you.
Making little laughing sounds when something is silly or tickles.
When tears come out of your eyes because you are sad or hurt.
When the corners of your mouth go up because you feel happy.
The ha-ha sound you make when something is really funny.
Opening your mouth really wide and taking a big breath when you are sleepy.
The big ah-choo that bursts out of your nose.
Wrapping your arms around someone you love and squeezing gently.
Closing just one eye quickly to be silly or share a secret.
Using one finger to show someone where to look.
Using a shovel or your hands to make a hole in the sand or dirt.
Using your hands to move something away from you, like a swing or a door.
Grabbing something and moving it toward you, like a wagon or a rope.
Touching someone with your lips to show you love them.
How you feel on your birthday when everything is going great.
How you feel when your ice cream falls on the ground.
The hot mad feeling when someone breaks your favorite toy.
How you feel in the dark when you think there is a monster under the bed.
How you feel at bedtime when your eyes want to close.
How your tummy feels when it growls and wants food.
Feeling quiet and wanting to hide when you meet new people.
The jumpy wiggly feeling the night before a trip to the amusement park.
How you feel when friends pop out and yell at your birthday party.
Feeling crabby and cross, like when you wake up too early.
Being able to do something even when it feels a little scary, like a superhero.
Acting goofy and funny to make everyone laugh.
The color of a stop sign, a fire truck, and a ripe apple.
The color of the sky on a sunny day and the ocean.
The color of the sun, a banana, and a school bus.
The color of grass, leaves, and frogs.
The color of grapes and eggplants, made by mixing red and blue.
The light color of a pig, a flamingo, and cotton candy.
A perfectly round shape like a ball, a cookie, or the sun.
A shape with four sides that are all exactly the same length.
A shape with three sides and three points, like a slice of pizza.
The pointy shape that twinkles in the night sky.
The shape you draw to show love, like on a valentine card.
The opposite of small, like an elephant compared to a mouse.
Very very small, like an ant or a grain of sand.
Moving very quickly, like a race car or a cheetah.
Taking a long time to move, like a snail or a turtle.
How fire, soup fresh from the stove, and a summer day feel.
How ice cream, snow, and the inside of the freezer feel.
When a sound is really big, like a drum or a fire truck siren.
When there is almost no sound at all, like in a library.
How you feel after jumping in a pool or standing in the rain.
The part of the day when you wake up and eat breakfast.
The dark part of the day when the moon is out and you go to bed.
Not yesterday and not tomorrow, but the day happening right now.
Where you are when you hide in back of a tree so no one can see you.
Where your shoes are when they sit below the bed.
The dark shape that follows you on the ground on a sunny day.
The colorful arc in the sky after rain when the sun comes out.
Running as fast as you possibly can for a short distance, like a race.
Almost falling down because your foot trips on something.
Jumping out of the way quickly so a ball does not hit you.
Keeping three balls in the air by tossing and catching them over and over.
Rolling your whole body forward in a circle, head over heels.
Walking unevenly because one of your legs or feet hurts.
Walking with big stiff steps like a soldier in a parade.
The fast bouncy way a horse runs.
Sliding along the ground on your belly the way a snake moves.
Shaking side to side like jelly or a table with one short leg.
Bending your knees low to the ground, like a cat about to pounce.
Jumping suddenly onto something, the way a kitten attacks a toy mouse.
Standing on one foot without wobbling or falling over.
When your body shakes all by itself because you are very cold.
Sucking in a quick loud breath when something surprises you.
Raising your hand flat to your forehead the way a soldier greets a captain.
Using a ruler or tape to find out how long or tall something is.
Moving a spoon around and around in a pot or bowl to mix things.
Putting bottles and paper in a special bin so they can be made into new things.
Having a party with cake and balloons because something wonderful happened.
Copying exactly what someone else says or does, like a parrot.
Fixing something that is broken so it works again.
Adding lights, ribbons, or pictures to make something look pretty for a party.
Picking all the ripe fruits and vegetables from a farm in the fall.
Talking so quietly and unclearly that people ask you to repeat it.
Saying something suddenly and loudly because you are excited or surprised.
Telling important news out loud so everyone in the room hears it.
When two people keep saying the other one is wrong, back and forth.
Saying sorry to someone after you do something wrong.
Talking too much about how great you are or the cool stuff you have.
Starting to talk while someone else is still in the middle of speaking.
Making a story bigger than it really was, like saying the fish you caught was as big as a car.
The butterflies-in-your-tummy feeling before a big test or show.
The big warm feeling when you work hard and do something really well.
The sour feeling when a friend gets the exact toy you wanted.
When your face turns red because you tripped in front of the whole class.
The feeling when you try and try but the puzzle still will not work.
Really wanting to know how something works and asking lots of questions.
Feeling sure you can do something well, with no doubts at all.
The letdown feeling when the trip you were excited about gets canceled.
The sad feeling when you have no one to play with or talk to.
Way more than just mad, so angry your face turns red like a volcano.
So super tired you can barely keep standing after running all day.
When your brain feels mixed up and you do not understand what is going on.
The blah feeling when there is nothing fun to do and time moves so slowly.
The warm feeling of being glad for the good things and people you have.
Feeling quiet and peaceful inside, with no worries at all.
A stretched-out round shape like an egg.
A shape with six sides, like the little rooms bees build in a honeycomb.
A solid box shape with six square faces, like a dice.
A perfectly round solid shape like a basketball or a globe.
A shape like a soup can, round on top and bottom with straight sides.
A line that curls around and around, like a snail shell or a slinky.
Lying flat and level from side to side, like the line where the sky meets the sea.
Standing straight up and down, like a flagpole or a tall tree trunk.
Super duper big, like a whale or a mountain.
When something cannot be seen at all, like air or a ghost's best trick.
When you can see right through something, like glass or plastic wrap.
Easy to break if you drop it, like an egg or a glass cup.
Very very old, from thousands of years ago, like dinosaurs bones or the pyramids.
Exactly the same in every way, like twins you cannot tell apart.
When there is nothing inside at all, like a juice box after you drink it all.
A chunk of time that lasts ten whole years.
A very long chunk of time that lasts one hundred years.
Twelve o'clock at night, when Cinderella's magic ran out.
The very early moment when the sun first peeks up and the sky gets light.
Flipped so the top is at the bottom, like hanging from monkey bars by your knees.
Moving to the left or right instead of forward, like a crab walks.
Facing or moving the wrong way around, like walking with your back leading.
When you yell in a cave or canyon and your own voice bounces back to you.
The picture of yourself you see when you look in a mirror or still water.
The invisible force that pulls everything down to the ground when you drop it.
When colors or shapes repeat in the same order, like stripes on a zebra.
The steady beat in music that makes you want to tap your foot.
When an animal's colors help it hide by blending in with leaves or sand.
Staying on top of the water without sinking, like a duck or a beach ball.
